scope: Independent conversion-fidelity review of four identity-bound open-access sources for controlled-corpus text assessment. This QC grants no scientific acceptance, screening decision, registry authority, or publication authority.
method: Resolved each PDF through generated/source-acquisition/completion-20260921/oa-acquisition-results.json and compared it with the corresponding canonical identity-bound Markdown.
Rendered every PDF page with Poppler pdftoppm at 90 DPI, inspected complete contact sheets, and separately inspected pages carrying methods, figures, tables, or formulas at full rendered resolution.
Compared headings, reading order, image placeholders, tables, formulas, captions, and adjacent explanatory prose. Converter quality scores were not treated as fidelity evidence.
Computed PDF, canonical Markdown, and contact-sheet hashes with src.assess.artifact_verification.artifact_hash.

structure.headings: Title, numbered sections, references, and appendices occur in source order.
structure.reading_order: The two-column article is largely linearized in correct reading order.
structure.tables: Tables 1 and 2 retain text, but Table 1 loses its two example images. Table 3 and the Appendix A image grid are image placeholders.
structure.figures: Figures 1 through 5 and their subfigures are image placeholders. Captions and qualitative prose survive, but plotted values, entity positions, example images, and visual comparisons do not.
structure.formulas: Six displayed probability, association, and bias-score definitions are replaced by formula-not-decoded placeholders.

losses: The six displayed definitions needed to reproduce the three association scores and the aggregate bias score are absent.
Figures 2 through 5 lose the quantitative score values and entity-level distributions that support the central comparison of pre-training, language-context, and visual-context bias.
Table 3 loses the images and exact paired probabilities used to demonstrate predictions that override visual evidence.
Figure 1 and Appendix A lose the visual examples used to define and document the case study.
records.assessment: The prose supports the qualitative conclusions, but the missing formal definitions and quantitative visual evidence prevent complete text-only assessment of the method and results. Repair must transcribe the formulas and preserve the argument-bearing values or faithful structured descriptions from Figures 2 through 5 and Table 3.

structure.headings: All substantive sections remain in source order, although several numbered headings contain OCR-confused glyphs.
structure.reading_order: Single-column prose remains sequential across the article.
structure.tables: The PDF contains no substantive tables.
structure.figures: Survey pie charts are image placeholders, while each chart's response percentages and interpretation are stated in the adjacent Markdown prose.

losses: Eight image placeholders omit the publisher mark, survey pie charts, and licence graphic.
Several section headings have OCR substitutions such as ϭ and Đ, and list bullets contain stray glyphs.
The charts' color encoding and layout are absent, but their assessment-relevant values are repeated in prose.
records.assessment: The research question, small survey design, participant limitations, response values, discussion, and conclusion remain readable. The missing charts are redundant with adjacent numerical prose, so the representation is accepted for text assessment with cautious heading normalization and PDF consultation for visual presentation.
